name: Alexandria Small Business Development Center (Alexandria SBDC)
offer: Free, confidential one-to-one guidance plus workshops and training for startups and existing businesses, including help with registration, licenses and permits, loan applications, minority certifications, contracts and marketing. Bilingual consultants available.
who: City of Alexandria businesses and Alexandria residents
address: 625 N. Washington St, Suite 400, Alexandria, VA 22314

name: Community Business Partnership (CBP)
offer: Nonprofit one-stop resource center with small business classes, in-depth one-on-one counseling, a business incubation center with co-working space, and alternative financing as an SBA microlender for businesses that cannot get traditional loans.
who: Aspiring and existing small business owners, with a focus on low-to-moderate income and disadvantaged entrepreneurs including minorities, women and people with disabilities

name: Fairfax County Public Library
offer: Free business, finance and nonprofit research tools for company, industry and market research, business plan guidance, LinkedIn Learning and legal forms, plus Grants Research and Training Centers at the Reston, Sherwood and Tysons-Pimmit regional libraries.
who: Small and medium-size businesses, entrepreneurs and nonprofits with a Fairfax County library card
address: 12000 Government Center Parkway, Suite 324, Fairfax, VA 22035

name: George Mason University Small Business Development Center (Mason SBDC)
offer: No-cost one-on-one business counseling and workshops on business planning, strategy, financing, marketing and government contracting. A regional center of the Virginia SBDC network, with satellite offices in Manassas and Herndon.
who: Prospective entrepreneurs and existing small business owners
serviceArea: Fairfax, Arlington and Prince William counties; cities of Fairfax, Manassas and Alexandria; Town of Herndon

name: Loudoun County Public Library
offer: Free business research with a library card, including LinkedIn Learning courses, Morningstar and Value Line investment research, and legal and business forms, plus makerspaces, free public meeting rooms and business programs across 10 branches.
who: Loudoun County residents, students, workers and business owners (free library card)
address: 102 North Street NE, Suite A, Leesburg, VA 20176

name: Loudoun County Small Business Development Center (Loudoun SBDC)
offer: No-cost one-on-one small business coaching and education, including How to Start a Business workshops, Business Plan Boot Camp and 1 Million Cups, from start-up through growth.
who: Loudoun County entrepreneurs and small business owners
address: 43777 Central Station Dr, Suite 300, Ashburn, VA 20147

name: SCORE Northern Virginia
offer: Free, confidential one-on-one mentoring from experienced business owners and executives, plus workshops, webinars and online courses on starting, running and growing a business. Mentoring is available across Northern Virginia and online.
who: Aspiring and existing small business owners
cost: Free (mentoring is always free; some workshops low-cost)
serviceArea: Northern Virginia and the DC metro area

name: U.S. Small Business Administration (SBA), Washington Metropolitan Area District Office
offer: Federal small business help, including SBA funding programs and loan referrals, counseling through SBA resource partners, federal contracting certifications and disaster recovery assistance.
who: Small business owners and aspiring entrepreneurs in Northern Virginia
serviceArea: Arlington, Fairfax and Loudoun counties and the cities of Alexandria, Fairfax and Falls Church, plus DC and nearby Maryland

name: Virginia APEX Accelerator
offer: No-cost expert guidance for winning federal, state and local government contracts: one-on-one counseling on registrations, certifications, proposals and compliance, plus training events and a bid-match service. By appointment only.
who: Virginia businesses interested in pursuing or expanding government contracting

name: Women's Business Center of Northern Virginia
offer: SBA-funded Women's Business Center run by Community Business Partnership, with free and low-cost workshops and training, plus free one-on-one counseling for women starting or expanding a business.
who: Women entrepreneurs, including minority and socially disadvantaged women
cost: Free and low-cost (one-on-one counseling is free)

name: Business Finance Center at Community Business Partnership (CBP)
offer: Springfield-based SBA microlender offering microloans and small business loans starting at $1,000, plus financial education, training, and help applying for larger SBA-backed loans.
who: Startups, micro-enterprises and small businesses in Northern Virginia, especially underserved and underbanked owners
cost: Loans carry interest; counseling and training programs available

name: ECDC Enterprise Development Group (EDG)
offer: Arlington-based nonprofit and SBA microloan intermediary providing microloans of $500 to $50,000 (terms up to 5 years), business training and advisory services.
who: Refugees, immigrants, asylees and low-to-moderate-income entrepreneurs in the DC metro area
cost: Loans carry interest; $100 non-refundable administrative charge
serviceArea: Washington, DC metropolitan area including Northern Virginia

name: Latino Economic Development Center (LEDC)
offer: Microloans from $500 to $250,000 for businesses that struggle to get bank credit, plus free one-on-one business coaching and workshops in English and Spanish. Has an Arlington office and coaches at Arlington's BizLaunch.
who: Latino and other underserved entrepreneurs and small business owners, open to all
cost: Coaching and workshops free; loans carry interest (rates as low as 6.5% fixed APR listed)
serviceArea: DC metro area including Northern Virginia (Arlington)

name: Locus (formerly Virginia Community Capital)
offer: Community lender (Locus Bank and Locus Impact Fund) providing flexible lending, banking and credit enhancement for small businesses and nonprofits, with a focus on affordable housing, clean energy, food systems and community health in under-resourced communities.
who: Small businesses and nonprofit organizations, especially in under-resourced communities

name: Prince William County IGNITE Startup Grant Program
offer: Competitive county grant program awarding $25,000 to $100,000 grants to high-growth startups and tech companies located in or relocating to Prince William County, plus networking and masterclass education.
who: High-growth startups and entrepreneurs in or willing to relocate to Prince William County
cost: Free to apply; 50% company match required on awards
needsCheck: No open application round could be verified for 2025-2026 (confirmed rounds ran 2020-2023). Check the program page for current status before featuring.

name: Virginia Small Business Financing Authority (VSBFA)
offer: The Commonwealth's financing authority, offering direct loans (including a microloan program and Child Care Financing Program), loan guaranty and cash collateral programs that support bank loans, loan participation and bond financing.
who: Virginia small businesses and nonprofits that need financing beyond what traditional lenders will provide
cost: Loan programs; interest and terms vary by program
address: 600 East Broad Street, Suite 300, Richmond, VA 23219

name: eVA, Virginia's Electronic Procurement Portal
offer: The Commonwealth's online procurement system, where vendors register to sell goods and services to 700+ state agencies, colleges, universities and local governments, and to find and bid on solicitations.
who: Any business that wants to sell to Virginia state or local government
cost: Free vendor registration; transaction fees apply on orders

name: SBA Veterans Business Outreach Center (VBOC) at Old Dominion University
offer: SBA-funded center providing free business training, counseling, mentoring, certification guidance and resource referrals for veteran entrepreneurs, including Boots to Business programs.
who: Veterans, transitioning service members and military spouses starting or growing a business
serviceArea: Statewide Virginia and West Virginia (serves Northern Virginia)

name: Virginia Department of Small Business and Supplier Diversity (SBSD), SWaM Certification Program
offer: State agency that certifies businesses as SWaM (Small, Women-owned and Minority-owned) and DBE, which helps them compete for Commonwealth of Virginia contracts. Also offers free business development and outreach help, including a Northern Virginia business services manager.
who: Small, women-owned and minority-owned businesses in Virginia

name: Virginia MBDA Business Center (operated by Capital Region Minority Supplier Development Council)
offer: U.S. Department of Commerce MBDA center whose consultants provide technical assistance and business development services to minority business enterprises, including help accessing capital, contracts and federal procurement opportunities.
who: Minority-owned businesses (MBEs) in Virginia
needsCheck: Status uncertain: the center's former website domain has lapsed. Confirm current status with the operator (CRMSDC) before featuring.

name: Alexandria Chamber of Commerce (The Chamber ALX)
offer: Advocacy-based chamber with 890+ member businesses, providing networking, brand-building programs, events and guidance for the Alexandria business community.
who: Businesses doing business in Alexandria
address: 100 N. Pitt Street, Suite 208, Alexandria, VA 22314

name: Arlington Chamber of Commerce
offer: Membership organization of 600+ businesses offering networking, committees, educational programming, advocacy and an online business directory. Its Small Business Accelerator sponsors half of first-year dues for SWaM businesses.
who: Businesses and nonprofits in Arlington (open to businesses located outside Arlington)
cost: Membership-based (dues vary by business size and industry)

name: Loudoun County Chamber of Commerce
offer: County chamber offering networking events, advocacy, educational programming, marketing exposure and a member directory for Loudoun businesses.
who: Businesses of all sizes in Loudoun County
cost: Membership-based (dues based on number of employees)

name: Northern Virginia Black Chamber of Commerce (NVBCC)
offer: Regional chamber advocating for Black-owned businesses, with networking events, educational webinars, professional development, marketing opportunities and a member business directory.
who: Black-owned businesses, entrepreneurs and supporters in Northern Virginia

name: Northern Virginia Chamber of Commerce
offer: The region's largest chamber (formerly the Fairfax County Chamber of Commerce), offering networking, legislative advocacy, professional development and business growth programs.
who: Businesses across Northern Virginia, from small firms to major employers
address: 7900 Westpark Drive, Suite A550, Tysons, VA 22102

name: Northern Virginia Hispanic American Chamber of Commerce (NOVAHCC)
offer: Bilingual multicultural chamber offering capacity building, access-to-capital support, curated networking and training to help member businesses grow revenue.
who: Hispanic and multicultural businesses and professionals in the DMV
serviceArea: Northern Virginia and the DC metro area

name: Prince William Chamber of Commerce
offer: The largest chamber in the DC metro area (about 1,300 members), offering business-building programming, advocacy, marketing visibility, member-to-member discounts and networking.
who: Businesses in Prince William County and the Cities of Manassas and Manassas Park
serviceArea: Prince William County, Manassas and Manassas Park

name: Virginia Black Business Directory (VABBD)
offer: Online, print and mobile-app directory of roughly 1,200 Black-owned businesses that helps consumers, buyers and partners find and support Black-owned firms.
who: Black-owned businesses seeking visibility; free for consumers to search

name: Virginia Black Chamber of Commerce (VABCC)
offer: Statewide chamber providing business development, grant and capital-access resources, technical assistance, networking, and the 360Forward entrepreneur and workforce pathways.
who: Black-owned businesses and entrepreneurs across Virginia

name: Alexandria Economic Development Partnership (AEDP)
offer: The city's economic development partnership, offering free one-on-one counseling, a Business Mentorship Program, the Accelerate ALX tech accelerator, startup checklists, site search and incentive guidance. Also hosts the Alexandria SBDC.
who: Businesses located in or moving to the City of Alexandria

name: Arlington Economic Development, BizLaunch
offer: Arlington's small business and entrepreneur support network, offering free one-on-one counseling in English and Spanish, workshops, market research, access-to-capital help and the BizLaunch PitchFest.
who: Entrepreneurs and small businesses in Arlington
address: 1100 N. Glebe Road, Suite 1500, Arlington, VA 22201

name: Fairfax County Economic Development Authority (FCEDA)
offer: County authority helping businesses start, expand or relocate, with a Business Diversity and Entrepreneurship team offering startup guidance, free SCORE mentoring, market research resources and referrals.
who: Businesses of all sizes in Fairfax County, including diverse and small businesses

name: Loudoun County Department of Economic Development
offer: County economic development department. Its Launch Loudoun program provides a startup guide, classes, funding and pitch-competition information, and connections to no-cost Loudoun SBDC advising.
who: Small businesses and entrepreneurs in Loudoun County
address: 43777 Central Station Drive, Suite 300, Ashburn, VA 20147

name: Prince William County Department of Economic Development
offer: County department running Calibrate, a small business resource hub covering every stage from idea to scaling, plus free consulting for existing businesses, incentive guidance and Mason SBDC counseling referrals.
who: Entrepreneurs and businesses in Prince William County

name: Mason Enterprise Center (George Mason University)
offer: George Mason University's incubator network, offering furnished offices and coworking, mentoring, business support services and the Mason SBDC's free counseling, with centers in Fairfax, Arlington and Herndon.
who: Startups and growing small businesses in Northern Virginia
cost: Fee-based office and incubator membership; SBDC counseling free
